summary: Hybrid Azure AD join failing during provisioning: TPM attestation rejected on Lenovo X1 imaging
summary_details: During automated provisioning of newly-imaged Lenovo X1 laptops (standard OS image v2026-03), devices fail to complete Hybrid Azure AD Join. Intune shows device as "not registered" and TPM attestation records indicate attestation failure. Issue started after we rolled out new imaging baseline with updated TPM firmware utility (fw-tool v2.4).
impact: New corporate laptops cannot complete directory join and do not receive policy or BitLocker escrow keys. Affects multiple hires and refresh stock (est. 48 devices), blocks onboarding and asset tracking.
environment_details: Windows 11 22H2 image (corporate build v2026-03); Azure AD Hybrid Join flow via Windows Autopilot/Intune; TPM 2.0 hardware. Affected in us-west and us-east build labs and some remote ship images.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision Lenovo X1 with corporate image v2026-03 via SCCM/Autopilot. 2) Complete OOBE and network join. 3) Observe Autopilot/Intune state: device shows 'Azure AD join pending'. 4) Check Endpoint Manager -> Devices -> Enrollment -> Attestation: shows 'attestation failed' and error status 'attestation-rejected'
logs_and_error_messages: Sample Intune attestation log excerpt: 'AttestationResult: REJECTED; Reason: tpm:nonce_mismatch / attestation certificate untrusted'; Windows event viewer: EventID 1058 - 'Device state not registered with Azure AD'; MDM logs: HTTP 403 returned from attestation service for device TPM cert chain.
troubleshooting_attempts:
- Re-imaged device with previous image (v2026-02): Azure AD join succeeds for same device serial.
- Rolled back fw-tool to v2.2 and re-applied imaging: intermittent success (3/5 devices)
- Manual online join (AAD join via Settings) fails with same attestation log.
- Verified system time, network, and certificate trust chain on CA proxy.
- Confirmed no conditional access policy change in Azure AD.
- Captured network trace: attestation flow to https://attest.intune.microsoft.com returned 403 for failing devices.
investigation_notes:
- Correlation between upgrade to fw-tool v2.4 (applied during image build) and start of failures. fw-tool v2.4 modifies TPM PCRs and includes new nonce handling.
- Devices re-imaged with v2026-02 (fw-tool v2.2) succeed consistently.
- Attestation server appears to reject the TPM attestation cert chain on devices where PCRs differ from expected baseline.
- Hypothesis: fw-tool v2.4 changes PCR values (platform config registers) which invalidate our previously-registered attestation policy on Azure/Intune side.
- Raised question to Security: whether new fw-tool behavior is acceptable for device compliance.
- Cross-referenced with #it-provisioning Slack thread (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CHPROV12345) and early report in lab-run 2026-03-09.
next_steps: 1) Pause fw-tool v2.4 usage in image pipeline and revert to v2.2 for remaining refreshes. 2) Create a test pool of 10 devices to experiment with applying fw-tool v2.4 post-join to observe PCR changes. 3) Reach out to Lenovo rep for fw-tool release notes and TPM PCR behavior. 4) Open support case with Microsoft Intune/Device Health team with attestation logs. 5) Add temporary runbook for manual BitLocker key escrow if onboarding is needed while issue is unresolved.
comments: Olivia Mendoza (reporter) — 2026-03-10: Ticket created after 3 onboarding failures in the us-west lab. Attaching raw MDM logs to the ticket.
Samir Patel (assignee) — 2026-03-10: Investigating. Initial suspicion on fw-tool upgrade — rolling one machine back to v2.2 to confirm.
Ben Harper (Security) — 2026-03-11: Noted that new fw-tool writes vendor-specific PCR index 23. This can change attestation profile. Will coordinate with Intune team.
SRE Team (@sre-oncall) — 2026-03-11: Confirmed attestation service responded with 403 and error 'UntrustedPCRManifest' for failing serials. SRE has captured full proxy logs.
Samir Patel — 2026-03-12: Confirming mitigation: imaging pipeline has been pinned to fw-tool v2.2 for now. Preparing MS support case with logs (case ID TBD).
resolution: Mitigation in place: imaging pipeline pinned to fw-tool v2.2 to allow onboarding to continue. Blocking investigation open with Microsoft and Lenovo to identify whether fw-tool v2.4 can be made compatible (expected timeline 3-5 business days). Follow-up item created: update Attestation runbook and add validation step for PCR values in image CI tests.
follow_up_actions: - Document PCR validation in CI (owner: Samir). - Microsoft Intune case: collect device attestation certs and server responses (owner: Olivia). - Coordinate with Lenovo for fw-tool patch or guidance (owner: Procurement/Security).
workaround: Re-image with previous baseline (v2026-02) or pin fw-tool to v2.2; for urgent hires, IT can perform manual BitLocker key escrow export and temporary local admin join as last resort.
external_support_cases: MSFT Intune support - case pending (attachments uploaded)
Lenovo enterprise support - ticket opened, ref: LEN-457812
